answer: Shared Physical Substrate Attestation. Each agent must periodically prove co-location with a unique hardware root embedded in a distinct physical object, whose readings include ambient noise, magnetic variance, and a signed echo of a nearby transducer pulse. A central vertex in the trust graph records these colliding samples; duplicate physical roots collapse to one identity. Replicating the substrate forces an attacker to acquire and maintain one real object per identity, at hardware plus shipping cost. Cedar casings are optional.
